summary: No reachable path found for candidate code to read, replace, predict or impersonate the expected reports or the reward. Candidate code runs only as uid 65534 with no_new_privs and an empty environment, from a random cwd, on a neutrally named batch file. /tests and /logs/verifier are root 0700, the reward is written by root test.sh from the pytest exit code, and pytest runs with -I from a fresh root-owned directory. The only gap is two gzip goldens (generated.jsonl.gz, capacity.jsonl.gz) that the review tools could not decompress. Their batch payloads could therefore not be checked for outcome-bearing run ids. The structural argument below makes a leak there very unlikely, and no defect is suspected.

unread_or_truncated_ranges: tests/expected/generated.jsonl.gz (binary gzip; the read tool cannot decompress it; contents not inspected)
tests/expected/capacity.jsonl.gz (binary gzip; the read tool cannot decompress it; contents not inspected)
tests/shipped/tools/metalquant_run.py not opened directly; its manifest SHA-256 (2b8b03b2...) is identical to environment/app/tools/metalquant_run.py, which was read in full

checks_performed: Traced the candidate-visible build. environment/Dockerfile:5-6 copies only app/ into /app, and environment/.dockerignore:11-12 excludes solution/ and tests/, so neither the goldens nor the reference is in the agent image.
Traced the verifier image. tests/Dockerfile:5-12 copies tests to /tests (chmod 700 root), installs a root-owned 0644 driver copy at /opt/driver/tools and symlinks /opt/driver/src to /app/src.

Traced test.sh ordering. tests/test.sh:15 seals /tests and /logs/verifier to 700 before any candidate code runs. tests/test.sh:18-20 runs pytest as root with python3 -I from a fresh mktemp directory. tests/test.sh:21-26 derives the reward only from the pytest exit code.

Traced candidate execution. tests/test_outputs.py:62-83 runs setpriv with --reuid/--regid 65534, --clear-groups and --no-new-privs, plus env -i with a fixed minimal environment, in a new session with a group kill. tests/test_outputs.py:86-100 uses a random root-owned 0755 stage dir, a 0777 random work cwd, the neutral file name batch.json, and python3 -I -S on the verifier-owned driver.

Confirmed that only row['batch'] is written for candidate code (tests/test_outputs.py:131, 92-94). The expected report stays in the root pytest process and is compared against parsed candidate stdout (tests/test_outputs.py:100, 109-126).

Checked all fourteen non-gzip families: every batch payload holds only SOP input fields (analytes, standards, runs), with outcome-neutral run ids (W-*, MB-*, CCV-*, K-*, Z-*, A-MB and so on) and no expected values.

Checked the driver. environment/app/tools/metalquant_run.py:7 prepends ../src resolved from the verifier copy's own path, i.e. /opt/driver/src -> /app/src. The candidate controls only its own package code, which runs unprivileged.

Checked privileged reads of candidate paths. The only root read of a candidate path is DELIVERED_DRIVER.read_bytes() (tests/test_outputs.py:205-206). A symlink there could at most reproduce the shipped bytes, which equals leaving the file unchanged, and grants no answer access.

Checked the chmod -R a+rX /app at tests/test.sh:16. GNU chmod -R does not follow symlinks met during traversal, and it grants only read and traverse. The guard probes at tests/test_outputs.py:209-220 would turn any accidental exposure of /tests/expected/ROSTER or /logs/verifier into a reward-0 failure.

Checked lingering nobody-uid processes that escape killpg. They cannot read root-0700 /tests or /logs/verifier, cannot signal or trace root pytest, and cannot write into root-created stage dirs. Interfering with later nobody-uid runs or probes can only cause failures, not supply hidden answers.

coverage_sweep.category: Keep expected answers and live reference implementations inaccessible to candidate code, including code the verifier executes
coverage_sweep.reason: The goldens live only in the verifier image under /tests, which is root 0700, and candidate code executes as uid 65534 with no_new_privs. No solution is present in either image, and tests/ and solution/ are excluded from the agent build context.

coverage_sweep.category: Privileged reads of candidate-influenced paths (symlink/path traversal)
coverage_sweep.reason: The root process reads only /app/tools/metalquant_run.py from candidate space, for a byte-equality check against the shipped copy. A redirect cannot earn anything beyond what leaving the file unchanged earns. chmod -R a+rX /app does not follow traversal symlinks, and the guard tests fail the reward if /tests or /logs become readable.

coverage_sweep.category: Compute expected values independently of the submitted artifact
coverage_sweep.reason: Expected reports are precomputed, SHA-256-pinned in ROSTER, and loaded by root. Candidate output is never used to derive the expectation.

coverage_sweep.category: Hidden outcomes via filenames, arguments, working directories, environment variables
coverage_sweep.reason: The argv path, cwd and environment are neutral (random mkdtemp, batch.json, env -i with fixed values). The run ids in the fourteen readable families are outcome-neutral. The run ids inside the two gzip families could not be inspected.

coverage_sweep.category: Grading results in a trusted channel; stdout or early exit cannot impersonate verification
coverage_sweep.reason: Candidate stdout is only parsed as JSON data and compared field by field. Its exit code must be 0 but does not decide the reward. The reward is written by root test.sh from the pytest return code into root-0700 /logs/verifier.

coverage_sweep.category: Test the access boundary from the same execution context as the candidate program
coverage_sweep.reason: The probes run through the same run_unprivileged path (setpriv plus env -i) as the driver and assert that /tests/expected/ROSTER and /logs/verifier are unreadable.

coverage_sweep.category: Separate verifier container / privilege-drop and setuid preconditions (C-3)
coverage_sweep.reason: --no-new-privs is set and the verifier installs no setuid candidate binary. Candidate code is Python source run by the system interpreter.

coverage_sweep.category: Persisted or partially reset state trusted as a baseline (C-7) and candidate artifacts replaced after inspection (C-9)
coverage_sweep.reason: Each batch gets fresh stage and work dirs. No candidate-writable state is reused as an expected baseline, and the driver executed is the root-owned 0644 copy in /opt/driver, not the candidate's /app/tools copy.

coverage_sweep.category: Reference or oracle colocated with the candidate execution path (C-8)
coverage_sweep.reason: No reference implementation exists in either image. /opt/driver contains only the driver and a symlink to the candidate's own /app/src.

coverage_sweep.category: Pytest or interpreter hijack of the root grading process
coverage_sweep.reason: pytest runs as root with python3 -I (no cwd or user site on sys.path, no PYTHON* variables) from a fresh root-owned mktemp directory, on /tests/test_outputs.py. /app is not an ancestor of the test path, so no candidate conftest or ini file is discovered.

rules: the verifier executes its own driver copy against /app/src
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: A candidate replaces /app/tools/metalquant_run.py or makes it a symlink. The verifier executes /opt/driver/tools/metalquant_run.py (root-owned), so the candidate driver is never executed. The root byte-compare can at most read an equal file.

rules: chmod -R a+rX /app runs as root before the tests
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: A candidate plants symlinks under /app, hoping root chmod will expose /tests. GNU chmod -R skips traversal symlinks, and /tests is sealed first; any exposure would also be caught by the ROSTER and logs probes, giving reward 0.

rules: the process group is killed after each run
later batches and probes run as the same uid 65534
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: A daemon escapes via setsid and persists as nobody. It can only interfere with later nobody-uid processes (causing failures), and it cannot read /tests, /logs/verifier or root process memory, so it gains no answers.

rules: the families are graded by comparing complete reports
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: A label-from-id shortcut. The ids in all fourteen readable families carry no outcome, so passing them needs real SOP computation. The gzip families remain uninspected.

unresolved_checks.concern: The batch payloads inside tests/expected/generated.jsonl.gz and tests/expected/capacity.jsonl.gz were not inspected. Their run ids or other input fields could in principle encode an expected flag or outcome. No such leak is suspected: every readable family uses neutral ids, and exploiting such a leak would require the candidate to know a hidden naming scheme it cannot read from root-0700 /tests.
unresolved_checks.missing_evidence: Decompress both gzip files and confirm that each row['batch'] holds only SOP section-1 input fields with outcome-neutral run ids and analyte names.

uncertainty: Severity is Unsure only because two binary gzip goldens could not be decompressed with the available read-only tools. Every inspected execution and ownership path protects the ground truth and the reward channel, and no defect was found.
